records.text: B'nai B'rith became the Anti-Defamation League after the murder of Mary Phagan.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: That then subsequently became the ADL after the ritualistic murder of a Catholic girl named Mary Phagan. There was no hiding that anymore.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The ADL's own 1913 founding charter and historical accounts show it was founded under B'nai B'rith before Leo Frank's August 1915 lynching. The Frank case influenced the organization's early context and growth, but the ADL did not come into existence after the murder.

sources.title: Anti-Defamation League Founding Charter (1913)
sources.relevance: Primary organizational document directly dates the ADL's founding to 1913, contradicting the claim that it arose after the 1915 murder.

records.text: B'nai B'rith has been running the United States since at least the Civil War.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Again, it was my independent study into Sigmund Freud that led me to learning about B'nai B'rith, the Jewish Freemason group who I believe have been running our country since at least the Civil War.

verification.notes: Context reviewed at 11:14, including the speaker's explicit 'I believe' qualifier. Current organizational histories confirm B'nai B'rith was founded in New York in 1843 and used a lodge structure, but no reliable evidence verifies the sweeping allegation that it has run the United States since the Civil War.

records.text: Candace Owens said Gary Javitch had been executive director of B'nai B'rith International for years, had served repeatedly as executive board chair, and received its inaugural President's Award in 2019
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: But most critically, what is something that you should know about Gary Javitch? He is—and he has been—the executive director of B'nai B'rith International for years. ... Anyway, back to Gary (Gary Javitch). He served on the B'nai B'rith International's board as their executive board chair in 2011, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019. ... He received the inaugural President's Award in 2019 for advancing the organization's mission.

verification.notes: B'nai B'rith records support Javitch's international executive-board service and 2019 President's Award, and other reporting identifies him as director of the Omaha lodge. However, official reports name Daniel Mariaschin—not Javitch—as B'nai B'rith International's executive vice president/CEO, so the statement incorrectly elevates a local director and board member to international executive director.

records.text: Candace Owens said B'nai B'rith was founded by German Jews as a Freemason lodge
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Yes, B'nai B'rith was indeed founded by German Jews. It was a Freemason lodge where Sigmund Freud, as we learned in one of our books, was free to denigrate the Goyim in his correspondence with his fellow Jews.

verification.notes: B'nai B'rith's own history confirms founding in New York in 1843 by twelve Jewish immigrants from Germany. The Holocaust Encyclopedia describes it as a Jewish fraternal organization created partly because Jews experienced exclusion from existing lodges; that does not establish that B'nai B'rith itself was a Freemason lodge. The founder-origin portion is true, while the Freemason-lodge characterization is unsupported/misleading.

sources.title: B'nai B'rith — History
sources.relevance: B'nai B'rith source confirms the 1843 founding by twelve Jewish immigrants from Germany.

sources.title: Freemasonry — Holocaust Encyclopedia
sources.relevance: Authoritative history distinguishes Jewish fraternal organizations such as B'nai B'rith from Freemasonry.

records.text: Candace Owens accused Leo Frank of assaulting and murdering 13-year-old Mary Phagan and said he was convicted after trying to blame a Black janitor who worked at his factory
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And that happened when the extraordinarily wealthy Jewish man in Atlanta named Leo Frank, who owned a factory and was president of the Atlanta B'nai B'rith chapter, assaulted and murdered an impoverished 13-year-old Catholic girl named Mary Phagan. ... He was convicted of this crime, despite trying to blame it on a poor, illiterate Black janitor who also worked for him at the factory.

verification.notes: The episode verifies that Owens made the accusation, and Library of Congress sources confirm Frank's conviction for Mary Phagan's murder and the central role of janitor Jim Conley's testimony. But the categorical assertion that Frank assaulted and murdered Phagan exceeds what current authoritative history supports: the Library of Congress describes a sensational, flawed trial, prejudice, uncertainty about guilt, and later evidence supporting innocence. This result preserves the distinction between conviction and proven guilt.

sources.title: Trial and Lynching of Leo Frank — Library of Congress
sources.relevance: Confirms the conviction and provides the case timeline.

sources.title: Confronting Challenges: The Lynching of Leo Frank — Library of Congress
sources.relevance: Describes the flawed trial, prejudice, uncertainty, and later innocence evidence.
